A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DDO work and contain readable main text and Appendices A–E. Equations, tables and figures can be matched across the bibliography expansion and shifted appendix pagination.

before.justification: v2 reports original DDO fine-tuning experiments on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet, including quantitative results in Tables 1–4, hyperparameter analyses and generated samples in Appendix E.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments, quantitative results, analyses and appendix samples. Their retention from v2 does not change their empirical status.

M1.justification: The likelihood-ratio discriminator, generalized DDO objective, diffusion approximation, multi-round refinement and VAR adaptation are unchanged. The new attention references suggest complementary acceleration without introducing a method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same unconditional and class-conditional CIFAR-10 tasks and ImageNet generation at 64, 256 and 512 resolutions. The added masked-language-model discussion does not introduce evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Tables 1–4 and the continued-MLE control in Figure 6 are unchanged. CMLM and the newly cited attention methods appear only in related work.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendix C retain the same 50,000-image FID evaluation, IS and NFE metrics, class-balancing practices, model configurations, training budgets and sampling procedures. Figure 6 retains its exception to class balancing.

E4.justification: The multi-round refinement, alpha/beta sensitivity, continued-MLE comparison and guidance trade-off analyses in Figures 6–7 are unchanged. Appendix E retains the same qualitative comparisons and refinement visualization.

E5.justification: Both versions retain point-estimate reporting without adding or removing repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4, the plotted results and Appendix E samples are unchanged. For example, EDM2-S + DDO retains ImageNet-64 FID 0.97, and VAR-d30 + DDO retains FIDs 1.79 without guidance and 1.73 with guidance in Table 4.

T1.justification: Theorems 3.1–3.3, their assumptions and Appendix B derivations are unchanged. The concluding sentence of the first optimality proof moves onto the next page; no mathematical content is added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about DDO's unified formulation, efficient refinement, generation quality and compatibility with guidance.

C2.justification: Appendix A makes the masked-case restriction explicit in its discrete-diffusion discussion; v2 already distinguished other variants in a footnote. It also specifies that numerical precision lowers effective temperature and affects generative-perplexity evaluation, replacing a more general criticism. DDO's own limitations and result interpretations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix C retains the same hardware, hyperparameters, precision settings, data-generation procedures and training times. Appendix D's code example and the supplied project link are unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds CMLM/Mask-Predict by Ghazvininejad et al. (2019) and four attention references: SageAttention, SageAttention2, SageAttention3 and SpargeAttn. It expands the masked-versus-autoregressive comparison and identifies attention acceleration as complementary to DDO. The central positioning relative to GANs, DPO and guidance remains intact.

P1.justification: The revision locally rewrites and expands Appendix A, renumbers and reorders affiliations, and changes the conference edition from 41st to 42nd. The main narrative and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The bibliography reflows onto an additional page, shifting the appendices, and Appendix A's expansion pushes a proof sentence across a page boundary. Figures 1–18 and Tables 1–4 retain their displays, captions and structure.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves contextual clarity in Appendix A by bringing the masked-case qualification into the main paragraph, specifying the temperature/perplexity issue and adding the CMLM precedent. These are limited gains in precision and context; the method, empirical support, proofs and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
